claims.text: The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a single-phase, dendritic BCC microstructure.
The baseline alloy has approximately 800 MPa yield strength and roughly 40% strain at lower temperature.
At 1273 K, the baseline alloy has approximately 330 MPa yield strength and 423 MPa compressive strength at 30% strain.
The proposed intervention is to add 1–3 at% Hf and approximately 0.5–1.5 at% C to TiVNbTa.
Hf is a strong carbide-forming element.
Homogenization of the Hf- and C-modified alloy will promote formation of fine HfC precipitates.
The resulting HfC precipitates will be thermally stable and distributed within the BCC matrix at 1273 K.
Dispersed HfC particles will strengthen the alloy by impeding dislocation motion and restricting dislocation glide at elevated temperature.
The HfC precipitates will prevent grain-boundary sliding.
Precipitation strengthening is a viable general strategy for improving the elevated-temperature strength of high-entropy alloys.
Grain refinement and precipitation strengthening have improved the compressive properties of a refractory NbMoTaWVTi alloy.
An Hf-containing HfMoNbTaW refractory alloy has demonstrated high yield strength at elevated temperature.
The modified TiVNbTa alloy will have a yield strength exceeding approximately 450 MPa at 1273 K.
The modified alloy will maintain ductility comparable to that of the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will preserve adequate heat-transfer capacity for use between W and CuCrZr.
The proposed strengthening effect will remain effective up to approximately 1273 K under compression to about 30% strain.
A vacuum or inert atmosphere will minimize oxidation during service or testing.
Prolonged exposure or temperatures above 1273 K may require additional oxidation protection or precipitate stabilization.
Precipitate size, precipitate volume fraction, and mechanical gains will depend on processing, composition control, and thermal exposure.
Failure to exceed 330 MPa yield strength at 1273 K or failure to form stable carbide precipitates would falsify the hypothesis.
